title: The Earliest and Latest Rounds Where Players Compete
summary: In a tournament with n players numbered from 1 to n, players compete in rounds where the i-th player from the front competes with the i-th player from the end.
statement: In a tournament with n players numbered from 1 to n, players compete in rounds where the i-th player from the front competes with the i-th player from the end. If the number of players is odd, the middle player automatically advances. Players numbered firstPlayer and secondPlayer are the best and can win against any other player before competing against each other. Return an integer array containing the earliest and latest possible round numbers in which firstPlayer and secondPlayer will compete against each other.
constraints: Each round pairs players symmetrically from the ends; an unpaired middle player advances.
The two named players always defeat others, while every other match outcome may vary; return earliest and latest possible meeting rounds.
hints: Only the ordered positions of the two protected players and the current field size affect future possibilities.
Enumerate winners of unrelated symmetric matches while forcing both protected players to advance.
Map their positions among sorted winners, memoize that smaller state, and combine child earliest/latest rounds.
Every legal round outcome produces one mapped state and every mapped state is explored; memoized recursion therefore spans exactly all possible brackets.
editorial: Every legal round outcome produces one mapped state and every mapped state is explored; memoized recursion therefore spans exactly all possible brackets.

tests.explanation: Across possible outcomes of other matches, the two players can first meet in round three or as late as round four.
The two players are paired from opposite ends in the opening round.
